## ⛔ First: my card body was wrong, and the dev measured rather than trusting it

I wrote this card's brief, and in it I listed the effect's `dataConfig` read set as including `:504`'s `dataConfig?.provider === 'object' ? dataConfig.object : undefined`. **That line is the `headerObjectName` read, which sits outside this effect.** The dev re-derived the read set **from the effect body** and found the real one: `provider`, and conditionally `object` / `items`.

⭐ My own dispatch order said *"re-derive the real read set, do not trust that list"* — and the reason it said so is that I did not fully trust my own enumeration. Good that the instruction was there; better that the dev acted on it rather than treating a PM-written list as measured. ⚠️ **A card body written by this seat is evidence about when it was written, exactly like anyone else's.**

## ⭐⭐ The #6592 trap was checked, not merely avoided

This was the one thing I flagged hardest, because #6592's ablation was bitten by it: its `ObjectCalendar` trigger passed even pre-fix, since that component's memo was *already* primitive-keyed by #6018 and the trigger never forced a recompute.

The dev verified the trigger against **this** component's actual memo before trusting it:

> `dataConfig = useMemo(() => getDataConfig(schema), [schema])` — keyed on the **whole schema object**, so a schema-reference swap reliably forces a recompute.

⇒ The trigger was shown to be capable of firing here *before* the zero it produces was believed. That is the difference between a discard pin and a dead pin, and it is now a checked property rather than an assumed one.

## The ablation

Both legs matched prediction with no direction surprise:

- **Mutation** — reverted `ObjectTree.tsx` to its pre-fix content, confirmed on disk by anchored `grep -c` (pre-fix deps-array marker 1 hit, post-fix `dataProvider` marker 0 hits), rebuilt `dist`, ran the pin: **RED**, `AssertionError: expected 2 to be 1`.
- **Restoration** — proven **byte-identical** by an empty `git diff HEAD` **and** a matching `git hash-object` (`94ba6dce…` on both sides), rebuilt, re-ran: **GREEN**.

⭐ Note the rebuild on both legs. This component's pin reads through `dist`, so a leg that skipped the rebuild would have measured the previous build — the dev rebuilt on each side rather than assuming the source edit was what the test saw.

⭐ Lint narrowing proved the right way: population **read from eslint's own `--format json`** (2 files), 0 errors, and the warning counts **compared against the pre-fix source** rather than merely reported — plus the invariance argument (no `parserOptions.project` / `projectService` anywhere, so type-aware linting is off repo-wide and this diff cannot move an untouched file's verdict).

## What this closes

⭐ This was the **last `dataConfig`-identity dependence in `ObjectTree`** — the schema-resolution half was already retired by #6696's `useSettledSchema` adoption. So the component is closed, not just the effect, and #6592's census no longer names a member it left behind.

Changeset `patch`, per the presence gate's own verdict. Fence clean: `packages/plugin-tree` only.
